spans.s:
ध्रु 1. ध्रु (connected with rt. धृ), cl. 1.
6. P. ध्रवति, ध्रुवति, दुध्राव, &c., to
be firm or fixed, to stand firm; to go, move; to ascer-
tain, know with certainty; to kill: Caus. ध्राव-
यति: Desid. दुध्रूषति, दुध्रुविषति: Intens.
दोध्रूयते; [cf. Lith. drūtas, ‘firm;’ Goth. traua,
‘I trust,’ = Caus.]

ध्रु 2. ध्रु (said to be fr. rt. ध्वृ) in
अ-स्मृत-ध्रु, not disappointing desire; (Sāy.) not
remembering injury.

ध्रू ध्रू, cl. 6. P. ध्रुवति, &c., = rt. 1.
ध्रु and ध्रुव्.

ध्रुति, इस्, f., Ved. (Sāy.) fixed destiny, settled course
of fate; (according to modern scholars) misleading,
leading astray, corrupting, seduction, (fr. rt. ध्वृ.)

ध्रुव, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed, firm, remaining fixed
in one place, firmly fixed, fast, immovable, stable,
[]
enduring, constant, lasting, permanent, continual, per-
petual, eternal, invariable, unchangeable, inevitable;
certain, sure, well-ascertained; firm, strong, fixed,
settle (as a day); fixed (in astrology, as a करण,
q. v.; the fixed Karaṇas are four, viz. Śakuni, Nāga,
Catuṣpada, and Kiṃstughna or Kintu-ghna (?): the
seven A-dhruvāṇi are given under करण: some of
the Nakṣatras are also called Dhruvāṇi, see नक्ष-
त्र); fixed (in anatomy, as certain members or
organs of the body which cannot be severed without
causing death, those which are separable being called
अ-ध्रुव, q. v.); tenacious, retentive (e. g. ध्रुवा
स्मृतिः, a retentive memory); (अस्), m. the polar
star or the north pole itself (personified in mythology
as son of Uttāna-pāda and grandson of the first
Manu); the pole of any great circle (especially either
of the celestial poles); polar longitude, the distance
of a planet from the beginning of the sidereal zodiac;
a constant arc; N. of one of the twenty-seven
astronomical Yogas or the Yoga star of the twelfth
lunar asterism (supposed to = ß Leonis?); a knot (?);
the trunk of a lopped tree or pollard, a post, stake;
the Indian fig-tree; the tip or point of the nose (?); a
sort of bird, = शरारि, (perhaps incorrectly for स्म-
रारि, meaning Śiva); the introductory stanza of a
poem or song (‘the constantly recurring verse,’ which
is repeated as a kind of burden or chorus); time,
epoch, era, any fixed period from which dates are
computed; an epithet of Brahmā; of Viṣṇu [cf.
ध्रुवाक्षर]; of Śiva; N. of one of the serpents
supporting the earth; N. of one of the Vasus; of a
son of Vasu-deva and Rohiṇī; of an Āṅgirasa, sup-
posed to be the author of a Ṛg-veda hymn (Ṛg-
veda

); of a son of Nahuṣa; of a hero on
the side of the Pāṇḍus; of a son of Ranti-nāra (or
Ranti-bhāra); (आ), f. the largest of the three sacri-
ficial ladles (made in the shape of the Indian fig-leaf
and of the wood of the Flacourtia Sapida?); the plant
Desmodium Gangeticum; the plant Sanseviera Zey-
lanica, a small tree from the fibres of which bow-
strings are made (= मूर्वा); a virtuous woman; a
cow which stands quiet when milked; scil. दिश्, the
point of the heavens directly under the feet, the
point of the lower hemisphere directly opposite to
the zenith; (अम्), n. ‘the enduring sound,’ a sound
heard or supposed to be heard after the Abhinidhāna,
probably the mere prolongation of the preceding
sound; heaven, sky, atmosphere; (अम्), ind. cer-
tainly, surely, assuredly; eternally; (आय), ind. for
ever. (According to grammarians, ध्रुव at the
end of a comp. may give a bad sense to the word
with which it is compounded, Pāṇ.

); [cf.
Hib. dearbh, ‘sure, true;’ Goth. triggvs; Angl.
Sax. treowe, for-truwyan; Old Germ. triu, triuwi,
ga-triu, ga-triuwi, ga-triwi, = Mod. Germ. treu,
treue, ge-treu, = Eng. true, trusty.]
—ध्रुव-केतु,
उस्, m. a kind of meteor.
—ध्रुव-क्षित्, त्, त्, त्,
Ved. resting firmly, abiding fixedly; abiding in the
fixed (sacrifice).
—ध्रुव-क्षिति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved.
having a firm position or abode.
—ध्रुव-क्षेम,
अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. abiding in fixed habitations, having
enduring mansions; firmly fixed.
—ध्रुव-गति,
इस्, f. a firm position; (इस्, इस्, इ), going firmly.
—ध्रुव-चरित, अम्, n., N. of the twelfth and
thirteenth chapters of the Svarga-khaṇḍa or third
part of the Padma-Purāṇa; N. of the sixty-second
chapter of the Liṅga-Purāṇa; of a chapter of the
Purāṇa-sarva-sva.
—ध्रुव-च्युत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. caus-
ing to fall or shaking the immovable (mountains).
—ध्रुव-तारा, f. or ध्रुव-तारक, अम्, n. the
polar star.
—ध्रुव-पटु, उस्, m., N. of a king of
Vallabhī or Ballabhī; [cf. ध्रुव-सेन.]
—ध्रुव-
योनि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. having a firm resting-place.
—ध्रुव-रत्ना, f., N. of one of the Mātṛs
attending on Skanda.
—ध्रुव-लक्षण, अम्, n.
‘the mark of recurring stanzas,’ N. of a chapter
of the Purāṇa-sarva-sva.
—ध्रुव-सद्, त्, त्, त्,
Ved. resting on firm ground, abiding in a firm
place.
—ध्रुव-सन्धि, इस्, m., N. of a prince, son
of Su-sandhi or Su-ṣandhi and father of Bharata.
—ध्रुव-सिद्धि, इस्, m. ‘through whom conva-
[]
lescence is sure,’ N. of a physician at the court of
Agni-mitra.
—ध्रुव-सेन, अस्, m., N. of two Bal-
labhī princes; [cf. ध्रुव-पटु.]
—ध्रुवाक्षर
(˚व-अक्ष्˚), अस्, m. ‘fixed and eternal,’ epithet of
Viṣṇu.
—ध्रुवावर्त (˚व-आव्˚), अस्, m. the point
on the crown of the head from which the hairs radiate.
—ध्रुवाश्व (˚व-अश्˚), अस्, m., N. of a prince.

ध्रुवक, अस्, m. polar longitude; the trunk of
a lopped tree; a post, pale, stake; the introductory
or recurring stanza of a song, see ध्रुव; N. of
one of the attendants of Skanda; (आ), f. the intro-
ductory stanza and burden of a song [cf. धुवका];
N. of a woman.
ध्रुवि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. firmly fixed, firm.
